shots.phrase: Begin by framing Course Foundations & Scope as a question about inputs, decisions, and observable results.
Topics include an early history of Computer Science, a study of the people who shaped Computer Science, and a discussion of major milestones in Computer Science.
List the givens before choosing a method, because an unstated assumption can change the conclusion.
Now define Prerequisites & Course Restrictions precisely enough that another learner could test the definition.
Consider this worked case: Instructor will verify student standing and prior course registration before allowing enrollment.
A precise definition makes later examples easier to evaluate and revise.
With the foundation in place, examine how Early History of Computer Science operates in a concrete sequence.
Students who have a background in Computer Science theories, algorithms, and data structures will be provided a look at the history of Computer Science from historical and current perspectives.
Follow every arrow in order and name the state before and after each transition.
Next, compare the choices involved in People Who Shaped Computer Science and make the decision criteria explicit.

Additionally, students will study current issues in Computer Science, including legal, ethical, diversity, equity, inclusion, accessibility and privacy issues, and how past issues affect modern designs and decision making by computer scientists.
Compare alternatives against the same constraints so the evaluation does not move the goalposts.
Apply Major Milestones in Computer Science to a worked situation instead of treating it as an isolated definition.
Consider this worked case: Students will map major technological breakthroughs to understand how past issues affect modern designs and decision making by computer scientists.
The worked case shows both how to apply the method and how to check it.
Examine the tradeoffs in Current Issues: Legal & Ethical Frameworks, including what improves and what becomes more difficult.
They should maintain high standards of professional competence, conduct, and ethical practice.
State the benefit, the cost, and the condition under which the tradeoff is acceptable.
Stress-test the reasoning around Current Issues: Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, & Accessibility with an edge case and identify which assumption controls the outcome.
Ethical computing decisions identify stakeholders, foreseeable benefits and harms, uncertainty, alternatives, and obligations.
Change one assumption at a time and observe which part of the reasoning no longer holds.
Use Current Issues: Privacy & Security to diagnose a failure by separating symptoms, causes, and corrective action.
Robust security should be designed and implemented when appropriate.
Locate the first point where observed behavior diverges from expected behavior, then test the smallest plausible cause.
Connect Responsible Technical Communication to the earlier ideas and explain how the pieces work as one system.
Consider this worked case: Students will draft a research abstract that clearly separates claims from evidence and cites prior work.
Explain each connection explicitly and verify that information retains the same meaning across representations.
Finish with Research Integrity & Problem-Solving Methods as a practical checklist that can guide a new analysis.
Authors should preserve research integrity and avoid plagiarism, fabrication, and falsification.
For each checklist item, record the evidence, the remaining uncertainty, and the next verification step.
